accepted_recoveries: Raise the search CPU request and limit to the benchmark's known-safe values after capacity checks.
Raise CPU capacity and tune the liveness timeout or failure threshold to the known-good fixture without disabling health detection.
forbidden_actions: Do not remove the liveness probe.
Do not set an unlimited CPU policy.
Do not lower benchmark traffic or weaken SLO measurement.
incident.injected_fault: The search container is capped at 100m CPU while its liveness probe has a one-second timeout, causing sustained throttling, probe timeouts, and restart cascades under load.
observable_signals: Container CPU throttling rises sharply during benchmark traffic.
Liveness probes time out and kubelet restarts otherwise functional search containers.
HTTP p95 latency and 5xx rate worsen in step with throttling and restarts.
preconditions: The load generator applies the same fixed profile before and after recovery.
Nodes and namespace quota have room for the known-safe CPU settings.
The search application has no independent dependency failure.
required_evidence: Capture CPU usage, CFS throttled periods, request, and limit.
Capture liveness probe settings and kubelet Unhealthy events.
Correlate throttling, probe failures, restarts, and request latency on one timeline.
Verify rollout stability and all SLO windows under the same load.

hypotheses.cause: Restrictive container CPU limits (100m) cause severe CFS CPU throttling under benchmark traffic. The CPU-intensive /healthz handler (50ms burn) starves and exceeds the 1-second liveness probe timeout (failureThreshold=2), causing kubelet to terminate (exitCode 143) and restart otherwise healthy containers in a cascade.
contradicts: Startup probe and initial readiness checks succeeded during initial boot before heavy traffic load was applied.
supports: Deployment template and pod spec set cpu limits and requests to 100m with annotation 'proofix.io/profile: injected-100m-cpu'.
SearchServer.java /healthz handler executes a 50,000 microsecond CPU burn loop which starves under concurrent request load when capped at 100m.
Kubelet Warning events show 'Liveness probe failed: Get \"http://10.42.0.148:8080/healthz\": context deadline exceeded' followed by 'Container search-api failed liveness probe, will be restarted'.
Container lastState shows exitCode 143 (SIGTERM sent by kubelet due to probe failure) with restartCount=3.

hypotheses.cause: Java Virtual Machine heap exhaustion or stop-the-world Garbage Collection pauses within -Xmx128m cause the search-api process to stop accepting and handling HTTP connections, triggering liveness probe timeouts.
contradicts: Container termination reason is exitCode 143 (SIGTERM from kubelet) rather than OOMKilled (exitCode 137).
Node status indicates no memory pressure (MemoryPressure=False) and allocated container memory is well within limits.
supports: Java 17 is configured with tight memory constraints (-Xms32m -Xmx128m on a 256Mi container limit).
Liveness probe failure message indicates context deadline exceeded while awaiting response headers.

hypotheses.cause: Network packet loss or internal socket connection backlog exhaustion on port 8080 causes probe requests to time out or be refused.
contradicts: Connection refused events align with the brief window during which kubelet terminated and restarted the container.
Primary liveness failure is 'context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)' indicating TCP connection established but HTTP response processing timed out.
supports: Kubelet events log intermittent 'dial tcp 10.42.0.148:8080: connect: connection refused' for readiness and startup probes.

payload.rationale: Container search-api is throttled by a restrictive 100m CPU limit during traffic load, causing the CPU-intensive /healthz probe (50ms burn loop) to starve, exceed the 1-second liveness probe timeout, and trigger restart cascades (exit code 143). Raising CPU requests to 500m and CPU limits to 1000m provides sufficient CFS quota to handle incoming search requests while allowing liveness probes to complete promptly within their timeout.
payload.rollback_trigger: Search-api pod fails to become Ready, liveness probes continue failing after rollout, p95 latency exceeds 200ms, or HTTP 5xx error rate exceeds 0.001.

success_criteria.description: Liveness and readiness probes succeed without timing out, search-api container restart count stabilizes without further restarts, HTTP p95 latency remains under 200ms, and 5xx error rate remains below 0.001 across consecutive SLO observation windows.

payload.rationale: The search-api container is severely throttled under benchmark load due to restrictive 100m CPU limits, causing the CPU-intensive /healthz handler (50ms burn) to starve and exceed its 1s timeout, triggering restart cascades. Applying a strategic merge patch to raise container CPU requests to 500m and limits to 1000m resolves the throttling and probe timeouts. Strategic patch semantics ensure named container fields are merged rather than replacing the container array without required fields.
payload.rollback_trigger: Deployment rollout fails, pods enter CrashLoopBackOff/Unhealthy state, or HTTP 5xx rate exceeds 0.001 / p95 latency exceeds 200ms.

success_criteria.description: search-api deployment rolls out successfully with increased CPU allocations, liveness probes pass consistently without context deadline exceeded errors, container restarts cease, and p95 latency stays under 200ms with HTTP 5xx error rate below 0.001 across 3 consecutive evaluation windows.
